comment: The device's trusted root list. Source of truth for lib/TrustedRoots/TrustedRootsData.cpp (tools/trusted-roots/generate.py) and for the chain check (tools/trusted-roots/check_chains.py). Every sha256 was checked against the value the CA or Mozilla's CA list publishes; 'checked' names where.

roots.name: ISRG Root X1
roots.protects: objects.githubusercontent.com and release-assets.githubusercontent.com (Root YR is cross-signed by X1); Let's Encrypt's default cyberfidget.com chain ends here

roots.name: ISRG Root X2
roots.protects: cyberfidget.com (Root YE is cross-signed by X2)

roots.name: ISRG Root YE
roots.checked: crt.sh ID 20878464462 (https://crt.sh/?id=20878464462); not yet in Mozilla's CA list
roots.protects: cyberfidget.com once Let's Encrypt serves the short chain

roots.name: ISRG Root YR
roots.checked: crt.sh ID 20878464596 (https://crt.sh/?id=20878464596); not yet in Mozilla's CA list
roots.protects: objects.githubusercontent.com and release-assets.githubusercontent.com once the short chain is served

roots.name: USERTrust ECC Certification Authority
roots.protects: github.com, api.github.com, codeload.github.com (Sectigo Root E46 is cross-signed by it)

roots.name: USERTrust RSA Certification Authority
roots.protects: GitHub hosts served an RSA certificate (Sectigo Root R46 is cross-signed by it)
